name: sports_analytics
doc:
SPORTS ANALYTICS - the published models, sealed (issue #11, 2026-10-16: reach, down the domain list).
Through sports_analytics.SPORT_VERIFY: Bill James's Pythagorean expectation (750 runs for, 600 against, and the
even case), the Elo expected score at a 100-point gap, at equal ratings, and the 400-point gap that defines the
scale as ten-to-one, the Elo update for a win and for a loss at K = 32, and games behind (a five-game gap and a
tie). The Pythagorean exponent and Elo's logistic with its 400 are fitted conventions, CITED; the arithmetic is
SEALED. Idempotent.

sticks.question: Sports analytics - Pythagorean expectation, Elo, games behind
sticks.statement: A season's record is predicted from runs by a power law, a match by a logistic of the rating gap, and a standing by half the sum of two differences.
references: B. James, Baseball Abstract (1980s) - the Pythagorean expectation
A. E. Elo, The Rating of Chessplayers, Past and Present (1978)
FIDE Rating Regulations (2024), article 8 - the expected-score table and K factors

marks.claim: [Pythagorean expectation, SEALED] 750 runs scored, 600 allowed: W = 750^2 / (750^2 + 600^2) = 0.610 (sealed through sports_analytics.SPORT_VERIFY) - about 99 wins in 162. James's rule: a team's record follows from its run differential more faithfully than from its record so far.
[the even case, SEALED] Equal runs for and against give exactly 0.500 (sealed through sports_analytics.SPORT_VERIFY), whatever the exponent - the formula is symmetric.

[a 100-point Elo gap, SEALED] 1600 against 1500: E = 1 / (1 + 10^(-100/400)) = 0.640 (sealed through sports_analytics.SPORT_VERIFY). The stronger player is expected to score 64 percent - a win in nearly two games of three.

[the 400-point gap, SEALED] 1500 against 1900: E = 1 / (1 + 10^1) = 0.0909 (sealed through sports_analytics.SPORT_VERIFY). Four hundred points is DEFINED as ten-to-one odds - the 400 in the formula is the scale's unit, not a finding.
[a win, SEALED] 1600 beats 1500 at K = 32: R' = 1600 + 32 (1 - 0.640) = 1611.52 (sealed through sports_analytics.SPORT_VERIFY). The favourite gains little for doing what was expected.

[a loss, SEALED] The same player loses: R' = 1600 + 32 (0 - 0.640) = 1579.52 (sealed through sports_analytics.SPORT_VERIFY) - and loses 20.48 points, the surprise priced by the same expectation. Win and loss are not symmetric; expectation is the pivot.

[games behind, SEALED] A leader at 50-30 and a team at 45-35: GB = ((50 - 45) + (35 - 30)) / 2 = 5.0 (sealed through sports_analytics.SPORT_VERIFY): half the sum of the two differences, so a half-game is possible when the teams have played different numbers of games.
[a tie, SEALED] Identical records are 0.0 games behind (sealed through sports_analytics.SPORT_VERIFY).

[the models, CITED] The exponent 2 is James's original; the best fit for baseball is nearer 1.83 (and varies by sport) - a FITTED model, not a law. Elo's logistic with 400 and the K factor (FIDE uses 10, 20 and 40) are chosen conventions of a rating system. Cited as postulates: they work, so a prediction from them is inferred, never kept as fact; the standing is the fact.
marks.source: James, Baseball Abstract; Elo (1978); FIDE Rating Regulations (2024) art. 8

marks.claim: [on the one map] The three models are statistics (card_floor_statistics: a power-law share, a logistic expectation, an update that moves by the surprise) applied to the record of games. The Elo scale was built for chess (the chess stick holds the board; this stick holds the rating) and the probability stick holds the odds the 400 encodes.
marks.source: the one map; card_floor_statistics; the chess and probability sticks
